work_order.understanding:
QA failed one case, T-35, with BUG-1: four links below the 44px minimum touch target. I reproduced it exactly against a production build of 598cda8 — the same four measurements, to the pixel (/ A "Tabs" 35x24, /settings A "Tabs" 35x24, /sign-in A "Create an account" 129x16, /sign-up A "Sign in" 48x16) — and then fixed it and re-measured to zero undersized controls. So the reported defect is real, small and now understood.

The previous work order's diagnosis was NOT wrong, but it was incomplete in a way that would have produced a third failure, so I am rewriting it rather than patching the patch. v1's root_cause said "not a defect — the repository is empty by design", which was true and correct about the repository, and it went on to describe the plan's own three self-inflicted defects. It was right about all of them. What it did not do is check its own design against the engine it targets: v1 specified globals.css to declare the six spacing tokens as `--space-1: 4px` through `--space-8: 32px`, and listed `px-space-4`, `gap-space-3`, `mt-space-4` and 48 more uses of that family across 18 files. Tailwind v4 does not generate utilities from a `--space-*` theme namespace. `--space-*` is not a spacing namespace in v4; the spacing scale is `--spacing-*`. I confirmed this in isolation with the pinned tailwindcss 4.3.3: a `@theme` block containing `--space-3: 12px` and a markup file using `gap-space-3` emits NOTHING into the utilities layer, while the same block written `--spacing-space-3` emits `.gap-space-3 { gap: var(--spacing-space-3) }`. So all 51 spacing utility uses in this PR compiled to no rule at all. Every padding, margin and gap in the product was silently zero.

That is the real root cause and it is one line of CSS, not three JSX attributes. The consequence is visible in QA's own evidence: the top bar's three controls measured a 0px gap between them, not the `gap-space-3` (12px) the header asks for, and the cross-link sat flush against the submit button at 0px. docs/ui.md:225 states BOTH clauses in one sentence — "Touch targets are at least 44px by 44px, and no control is within 8px of another control's edge". QA's test only measures the first clause, which is why it reported the links and not the spacing. But the spacing is the underlying defect: it is why the links are crowded at all, and a fix that only added min-height to the three link call sites would have satisfied the one assertion QA happened to write while leaving the product with no spacing anywhere and the second clause of the rule still violated. I checked that empirically rather than assuming: with min-height added but the tokens still inert, the cross-link-to-submit-button gap measured 0px.

The second, independent finding is that min-height alone would not have fixed the links even with spacing working, because these are INLINE anchors. `min-height` does not apply to a non-replaced inline box. I verified this in Chromium: an inline `<a>` with `min-height:44px` measures 85x19 — the utility is silently discarded. Copying the siblings' exact `min-h-[44px] leading-[44px]` onto the cross-links, the obvious patch, leaves them 167x19. They need `inline-flex items-center` to become a block-level box the utility can apply to, and `min-w-[44px]` because QA asserts BOTH axes and the brand link is 35px wide. The brand link additionally needed `inline-flex` for the same reason even though it sits in a flex parent. I also tried and rejected `align-middle` on the cross-links: it is not needed once the spacing tokens resolve, and I removed it to keep the diff minimal.

Nothing in the previous order's design was arbitrary here — the token NAMES (`--space-1`, `gap-space-3`) were chosen to match docs/ui.md's spacing table by name rather than by count, which v1 was deliberate about and which is still the right instinct. The error is that the namespace prefix was carried from v3 syntax into v4. The fix keeps every class name in all 18 files exactly as written and changes only the six token declarations to the v4 namespace.
work_order.root_cause:
Two independent causes, and v1 diagnosed neither.

1. THE PRIMARY CAUSE, and the one v1 got wrong by omission: src/app/globals.css declares the six spacing tokens as `--space-1` … `--space-8` inside `@theme`. Tailwind CSS v4 generates no utilities from a `--space-*` theme namespace — the v4 spacing namespace is `--spacing-*`. Verified against the pinned tailwindcss 4.3.3: a `@theme` block with `--space-3: 12px` emits zero rules for `gap-space-3`, `mt-space-4`, `px-space-4` and the rest; the same token written `--spacing-space-3` emits `.gap-space-3 { gap: var(--spacing-space-3); }`. All 51 spacing utility uses across 18 files under src/ compiled to nothing, so every margin, padding and gap in the product was zero. This is why the top bar's controls sit 0px apart and why the auth cross-link touches the submit button — and it is why docs/ui.md:225's second clause ("no control is within 8px of another control's edge") is violated across the app even though QA only tested the first clause.

2. THE REPORTED SYMPTOM, whose obvious fix does not work: the three under-sized links (src/components/ui/top-bar.tsx brand link; src/components/auth-form.tsx:98 and :107 cross-links) are INLINE anchors, and `min-height` does not apply to a non-replaced inline box — Chromium measures an inline `<a>` carrying `min-height:44px` at 85x19, and the siblings' `min-h-[44px] leading-[44px]` at 167x19. They require `inline-flex items-center` to become a box the utility can size, plus `min-w-[44px]` because QA asserts both axes and the brand link is only 35px wide.

The two interact: with the tokens inert, adding min-height to the links still leaves them 0px from the submit button, so fixing only the links satisfies the assertion QA wrote while leaving the rule it derives from broken.
work_order.approach:
Four edits. The first is the whole fix; the other three make the three links actually reach 44px.

**1. src/app/globals.css — the root cause.** Rename the six spacing tokens from `--space-N` to `--spacing-space-N`, keeping every value and keeping the `space` infix. `--spacing-*` is the v4 spacing namespace, and `--spacing-space-3` is what generates the class name `gap-space-3` — the exact class names already written in all 18 files. No JSX changes, no class renames, no second token family: the existing markup starts working. Do NOT also add a parallel `--space-*` block or switch the call sites to bare `gap-3`/`p-4`; the v3 default spacing scale is already emitted by the Tailwind import, so bare numeric utilities would work too, but they would mean editing 51 call sites and losing the token-name-is-the-docs-table-name property v1 was deliberate about. One block, six lines.

**2–4. The three links.** Each gets `inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center` prepended to its existing classes. `inline-flex` is load-bearing and must not be dropped: without it these are inline boxes and min-height is discarded by the engine, which is the trap that makes the naive patch look like it worked. `min-w-[44px]` is load-bearing on the brand link, which is 35px wide and fails QA's width assertion otherwise. Do not add `align-middle` — measured, it is unnecessary once the spacing tokens resolve, and it is not needed for either clause of the rule.

**A test that reproduces the failure.** jsdom computes no layout and returns 0x0 for every element, so no unit test can assert 44px — tests/components/ui.test.tsx must instead assert the MARKUP that produces it: that the brand link and both auth cross-links carry the min-h and min-w utilities and are not bare inline anchors. That is the regression guard for the JSX half and it fails on the pre-fix source. The 44px and 8px assertions themselves are browser-only, which is exactly why AC-12 is written as a browser criterion: it is the only thing that will catch the CSS half, because the CSS half is invisible to every check CI runs.

**Verified before proposing.** I applied this exact four-edit change to 598cda8, built it, and measured in Chromium at the same four URLs QA used: zero undersized controls (was four), every control >=44px on both axes, inter-control gaps 36/12/16px on the auth screens and 12px across the top bar (was 0px), no horizontal overflow at 360px on any of the four screens, one h1 per signed-in screen, sign-up still lands on /, and vitest 81/81, tsc --noEmit and eslint all clean. The gap figures are the designed token values, which is the check that the tokens now resolve.

Deliberately NOT done: no change to any other component's classes. The 15 other files that use spacing utilities need no edit — they are fixed by the token rename alone, which is the point of fixing the cause rather than the symptom. No change to docs/ui.md or any other approved doc (reserved path). No dark mode, no new primitive.

files.change: In the @theme block, rename the six spacing tokens from --space-1: 4px, --space-2: 8px, --space-3: 12px, --space-4: 16px, --space-6: 24px, --space-8: 32px to --spacing-space-1, --spacing-space-2, --spacing-space-3, --spacing-space-4, --spacing-space-6, --spacing-space-8. Keep every value byte-identical and keep the `space` infix so the generated class names are exactly the ones already used in src/ (gap-space-3, mt-space-4, px-space-6 and the other 46 uses). Change nothing else in the file: the ten colour tokens, the radius, the font stacks, the five text sizes, the focus ring and the 480px card rule are all correct and all verified working. `--spacing-*` is the Tailwind v4 spacing namespace; `--space-*` is not one and generates no utilities at all, which is why all 51 spacing uses in this PR currently compile to nothing.
files.why: This is the root cause of the failure and it is the only edit that changes behaviour beyond the three links. It is invisible to tsc, eslint and vitest — all three were green on the broken build — and invisible to every layout assertion QA had not yet written, which is why it survived a full review.

files.change: On the brand link at line 17, prepend `inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center` to the existing `font-medium`, giving className="inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center font-medium". `inline-flex` is required: a next/link anchor is inline by default and min-height does not apply to a non-replaced inline box, so without it the utility is discarded and the link stays 24px tall. `min-w-[44px]` is required because QA asserts both axes and "Tabs" is only 35px wide. Change nothing else in the file — the two sibling links already carry min-h-[44px] leading-[44px] and measure correctly, and the header's own min-h-[44px] and gap-space-3 are correct.

On the two footer cross-links at lines 98 and 107, prepend `inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center` to each existing `text-primary underline`, so each becomes className="inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center text-primary underline". These are bare <a> elements inside the closing paragraph, so `inline-flex` is what makes them block-level enough for min-height to apply; with only min-h added they still measure 16px tall. Do not add vertical-align/align-middle — measured against the fixed build it changes nothing and the diff stays smaller without it. Change nothing else: the form, the fields, the busy state and the useActionState wiring are all correct and all covered by passing tests.

Add a describe block that renders <TopBar user={user} /> and asserts the brand link's className contains min-h-[44px] and min-w-[44px] — this is the regression test for BUG-1's top-bar half and it fails on the pre-fix source, where the className is exactly "font-medium". Add a second case for the auth cross-links asserting each carries the same three utilities and is not a bare inline anchor. jsdom computes no layout and returns 0x0 for every element, so this asserts the MARKUP that produces a 44px target, never a measured height; say so in a comment so a later reader does not think the assertion is weaker than it looks and go add a getBoundingClientRect call that would always return 0. Note in the same comment that the measured 44px and 8px properties are asserted only by AC-12 in a browser, because nothing CI runs can observe them.

cases: the top-bar brand link carries min-h-[44px] and min-w-[44px] in its className — fails on the pre-fix source, where it is exactly 'font-medium', and is the reproduction of BUG-1's first measurement
both auth-form cross-links carry min-h-[44px] and min-w-[44px] and are not bare inline anchors — reproduces BUG-1's second and third measurements
the assertion is on markup, never on a measured height, with a comment recording that jsdom returns 0x0 for every element and that AC-12 is the browser-side check

acceptance.check: On a clean checkout the dependencies install with scripts disabled, `npm run sdlc:verify` runs tsc --noEmit, eslint and vitest and all three exit 0, and `npm run sdlc:serve` builds and answers on port 3000. Every entry point that reaches config() declares itself local: sdlc:serve on both halves, `npm run dev`, `npm test` and a bare `npx vitest run` — so a developer with nothing set and a runner with nothing set both come up, and only a process that has not declared itself local is strict.
acceptance.how_to_verify: A clean checkout: `bash .sdlc/bin/install-deps.sh --ignore-scripts`, then `npm run sdlc:verify` (all three commands exit 0) and `npm run sdlc:serve` followed by `curl -fsS http://localhost:3000/api/health`. Then, with nothing exported: `npx vitest run` exits 0 and `npm run dev` starts and serves /sign-in. The second sentence is the regression guard for the environment policy and is what makes every browser criterion below reachable.

acceptance.check: GET /api/health returns 200 with { status, database, latencyMs } and a latencyMs greater than zero after a real query, and 503 with a fixed sentence when the database cannot be reached; a process that is not configured returns 503 with a different fixed sentence rather than claiming a database fault. No response, in any case, ever contains the connection string, a password or a host with credentials, and the message is never the driver's own text.
acceptance.how_to_verify: tests/integration/health.test.ts calls the route handler's GET directly against a fresh PGlite (200, positive latency), against a closed client (503, database sentence) and with an injected failing config (503, unconfigured sentence). QA curls the running app and inspects the body for credentials.

acceptance.check: With DATABASE_URL unset the application runs on in-process PGlite and applies the committed migration list on boot; setting it uses that Postgres with the same migrations; applying the list to an up-to-date database re-applies nothing, and a lock stops two concurrent cold starts applying one migration twice. A first boot on an empty database creates the migrator's own bookkeeping table rather than failing to read it.
acceptance.how_to_verify: tests/integration/migrations.test.ts on a fresh in-process PGlite with no DATABASE_URL anywhere in the environment, including the case where no bookkeeping table exists yet; plus `npm run sdlc:serve` and `curl /api/health` returning 200 with database:'ok', which is the PGlite path since the harness sets no DATABASE_URL.

acceptance.check: A person can sign up with an email and password at /sign-up, lands signed in on /, and sees the empty state 'You're not in any groups yet.' with a Create group action. Signed out, / redirects to /sign-in.
acceptance.how_to_verify: tests/integration/auth.test.ts for the transaction and the duplicate-email case; QA drives the real form in a browser against the sdlc:serve boot, which is the only place the landing page and its empty state can be seen.

acceptance.check: The password is stored only as a salted scrypt hash carrying its parameters, and only the SHA-256 of the session token is persisted: the raw cookie value appears nowhere in the database, the cookie is set httpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Lax with path /, and a session past its expiry is refused and its row deleted. The email and the source address are stored only as HMAC-SHA-256 under the configured secret, so no digest is computable without it.
acceptance.how_to_verify: tests/lib/auth.test.ts asserts the hash string carries N, r, p, the salt and the digest and contains no plaintext; that the sessions row holds the SHA-256 and not the token; that keyFor/sourceFor are keyed; and that the cookie attributes, read through src/lib/cookies.ts and tests/helpers/request.ts, are exactly httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax and path /. QA confirms the browser stores the Secure cookie over http://localhost and reports a browser that drops it rather than working around it.

acceptance.check: Signing out deletes the session row on the server and clears the cookie; replaying the old cookie afterwards is unauthenticated and / redirects to /sign-in.
acceptance.how_to_verify: tests/integration/auth.test.ts deletes the row and re-resolves the old token through the same cookieStore() seam. QA copies the cookie value before signing out, re-pastes it and opens /.

acceptance.check: The account limit refuses a wrong password once six failures for that key already exist in the window, so the seventh wrong attempt inside the window is refused, and a correct password is accepted regardless of the count. The source limit refuses once twenty failures from that source already exist in the window, so the twenty-first attempt inside the window is refused without verifying the password at all, and a request whose source address cannot be determined is exempt from that limit. Both predicates count failed attempts only. The status and response body for an unknown email are byte-identical to those for a wrong password, including when rate-limited.
acceptance.how_to_verify: tests/lib/auth.test.ts: checkRateLimit returns 'ok' at five failures for the key and 'account' once six already exist. tests/integration/rate-limit.test.ts: the seventh wrong sign-in is refused, adds no seventh row, and returns a result deep-equal to the first six's, and the correct password is then accepted; separately the twenty-first attempt from one address hard-refuses without calling the verifier, while a request with no determinable address does not. Both test files name the seventh and the twenty-first attempt — the boundaries this criterion fixes. The byte-identity half is deep equality of the three returned results and byte equality of the three rendered messages; the HTTP-status half is QA's, in the qa_script.

acceptance.check: At /settings a person edits their display name and default currency and saves; the new name appears everywhere the user is shown, including the top bar, and the currency is stored normalised to three uppercase letters.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Edit both fields at /settings in the running app, save, and confirm the new name in the top bar on / and on /settings. tests/integration/auth.test.ts covers the normalisation, the refusal of a non-three-letter value, and the authorisation check.

acceptance.check: With nothing set and TABS_ENV=local the app boots on documented local defaults — DATABASE_URL unset, a marked development-only HMAC key — and logs one line naming each default it used. With TABS_ENV unset or set to anything other than 'local', which is every boot that has not explicitly declared itself local, a missing required variable (DATABASE_URL or TABS_HMAC_KEY) stops startup with one message naming every missing variable and stating that TABS_ENV=local is the way out. NODE_ENV is not consulted anywhere in this decision: `next start` sets it to production on its own, so a check keyed on it can never distinguish a real deployment from CI or QA.
acceptance.how_to_verify: tests/lib/env.test.ts calls loadEnv with explicit environment objects for all three cases. The regression case asserts that importing the module with NODE_ENV=production and nothing set does not throw — it fails if anyone reintroduces either half of v1's mistake. Do NOT assert that the QA boot is a development boot: it is a production build, and it declares itself local through TABS_ENV, which is why every script that reaches config() carries that prefix.

acceptance.check: Every screen added here has exactly one h1, correct heading order, a label on every control, a visible focus ring at every tab stop, and designed empty, loading and error states per docs/ui.md.
acceptance.how_to_verify: tests/components/ui.test.tsx asserts the structural half on a real composition of the extracted components the pages render — <Shell user><HomeEmpty/></Shell> — which is the only composition that can prove 'exactly one' rather than 'at most one' per component. QA tabs each of the four screens against the running build for the focus ring at every stop, the single h1 and the three states, since the screens themselves are async Server Components that cannot be rendered by testing-library and whose import would construct a real database.

acceptance.check: Integration tests run against a fresh in-process PGlite with no network: the migrations apply to an empty database including the first-boot case, re-applying is a no-op, the health endpoint answers both 200 and 503, and the session and rate-limit rules above hold.
acceptance.how_to_verify: `npm test` on a runner with no DATABASE_URL and no Postgres installed; the suite passing at all is the proof, since every case would fail on a network dependency. The single sanctioned way a test reaches the database is tests/helpers/pglite.ts, which installs its instance before any module import — a test that reaches the client singleton any other way has built a defect, not a shortcut.

acceptance.check: Every visible control on /, /settings, /sign-in and /sign-up is at least 44px by 44px measured with getBoundingClientRect, including the links inside body text: the top-bar brand link, the two sibling navigation links, the sign-out control, the submit button, every input, and the cross-link that leads from one auth form to the other. No two visible controls sit within 8px of each other's edge, so a tap aimed at one control cannot land on the next. This is docs/ui.md:225, and it holds only because the spacing utilities resolve: a control is 44px tall by its own min-height, and the 8px separation between neighbouring controls comes from the gap and margin utilities actually producing their declared spacing.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Browser only, against the running build — this is the one property a jsdom test cannot see, because jsdom computes no layout and returns 0x0 for every element. Sign up, then on each of the four screens evaluate getBoundingClientRect() over every visible a, button, input, select and textarea, excluding sr-only clips, and assert each is at least 44 on BOTH axes; separately assert no two such controls are within 8px of each other's edge. The second assertion is the one that fails if the spacing utilities silently stop resolving, which is how this defect presented. tests/components/ui.test.tsx is the unit-level guard for the link markup: it asserts the brand link and both auth cross-links carry the min-h/min-w utilities and are not left as bare inline anchors.

qa_script: The app is already built and running on http://localhost:3000 by the pipeline through `npm run sdlc:serve`, which sets TABS_ENV=local. Confirm `npm run sdlc:ready` exits 0 before touching a browser. If it does not, stop and report blocked and paste the startup log line.

THIS TICKET'S CHECK, and it is the one that matters. On each of /, /settings, /sign-in and /sign-up, evaluate over every visible a, button, input, select and textarea (excluding sr-only clips): getBoundingClientRect(), and assert each is at least 44 on BOTH axes. BUG-1 was exactly this and it must now return an empty list. The four that failed were the top-bar brand link 'Tabs' at 35x24 on / and /settings, 'Create an account' at 129x16 on /sign-in, and 'Sign in' at 48x16 on /sign-up.

Then the second half of AC-12, which no previous QA run tested: on the same four screens assert that no two visible controls sit within 8px of each other's edge. The pre-fix build had the top bar's three controls 0px apart and the auth cross-link 0px from the submit button. The fixed build measures 12px across the top bar and 36/12/16px down the auth forms. If this fails, the spacing utilities are not resolving — that is the root cause, not a missing class.

Also on each of the four screens, sanity-check that spacing is visibly present at all, since the pre-fix build had none: the top bar's items are separated, the auth form's fields are spaced apart, and the submit button is not touching the cross-link below it.

Confirm no horizontal scrolling at 360px on any of the four screens, and that sign-up still lands signed in on / with the empty state and exactly one h1 — the CSS change touches every screen's box model, so the regression to watch for is layout, not auth.

Do NOT report as bugs in this ticket: the source-address rate limit being inert; the app booting on local defaults; sign-out living outside a profile menu; the money/dialog/skeleton primitives having no callers; or anything about groups, invites or amounts.
risks: The globals.css rename changes the box model of every screen at once — all 51 spacing uses across 18 files begin resolving where they previously produced nothing. This is the intended fix and it is measured green on all four screens, but it is the widest-blast-radius edit in the ticket by far, and it is the thing to re-check first if a future run reports a layout regression.

Two spacing utilities appear in the source with a bare value rather than the family form: `space-1`, `space-2`, `space-3`, `space-4`, `space-6`, `space-8` in globals.css's own comment block. Confirm on the built CSS that none of these is a real class in use; they are the token names inside a comment, not utilities, and the rename does not touch them.

`--spacing-*` also defines Tailwind's default numeric spacing scale, so a bare `p-4` or `gap-3` would now resolve where it previously did not. Nothing in src/ uses the bare numeric form (verified by grep), so this changes nothing today, but a later ticket writing `gap-3` by habit would get a value this theme block now influences.

If a future ticket adds a spacing token it must use the `--spacing-space-N` form. Writing `--space-N` reintroduces this exact defect silently: no type error, no lint error, no test failure, and a UI that is merely missing its spacing.
out_of_scope: docs/ui.md and every other approved doc — reserved path; the 44px/8px rule at :225 is already correct and is what the code must satisfy, not something to edit.
The other 15 files that use spacing utilities. They need no edit; the token rename fixes them. Editing them would be treating the symptom.

Adding a lint rule or a unit test that catches an unresolvable theme namespace. It would be genuinely useful, but it is a new guard with its own design questions, and the four edits here are what the failure actually calls for. Named here so the next ticket can take it deliberately.

The sign-out control sitting outside a profile menu, and the money/dialog/skeleton primitives having no callers — both were ruled out of scope by the previous order and QA was told not to report them.
Everything about groups, invites, expenses and amounts. This issue is the accounts-and-sessions skeleton.
work_order.confidence_rationale: High, because this is the rare root cause that is fully reproduced, fully explained and fully verified rather than argued. I built 598cda8, reproduced QA's four measurements to the pixel, isolated the Tailwind namespace behaviour against the pinned 4.3.3 to prove `--space-*` emits nothing, verified the inline-box min-height trap in Chromium (85x19 with min-height alone; 167x19 with the siblings' exact classes), applied the fix and re-measured: zero undersized controls, inter-control gaps now at their designed token values, 81/81 tests, tsc and eslint clean. Not 100 because the change is wide — the token rename alters the box model of all 18 files — and because the 8px-separation clause has never been exercised by any prior QA run, so I have established a baseline for it but not a long record of it holding across future changes.
evidence: Reproduced BUG-1 exactly against a production build of 598cda8 on http://localhost:3000, using QA's own undersizedTargets() predicate from spec/a11y.spec.ts:41. Output: /: A "Tabs" 35x24 · /settings: A "Tabs" 35x24 · /sign-in: A "Create an account" 129x16 · /sign-up: A "Sign in" 48x16 — identical to qa-evidence/touch-targets.txt, to the pixel.

Root cause isolated in tailwindcss 4.3.3 (the pinned version): a @theme block declaring `--space-3: 12px` with markup using `gap-space-3`, `mt-space-4`, `p-space-4`, `mt-4`, `gap-3` emits only `.mt-4` and `.gap-3` into @layer utilities — every `-space-` class produces no rule. Rewriting the same values as `--spacing-space-3` emits `.gap-space-3 { gap: var(--spacing-space-3) }` and `.mt-space-4 { margin-top: var(--spacing-space-4) }`.

The compiled stylesheet served by the app on the pre-fix build contains no `.mt-space-*`, `.gap-space-*` or `.px-space-*` rule at all (grepped /_next/static/chunks/*.css), while computed styles confirm it at runtime: the form's className is 'mt-space-4 flex flex-col gap-space-3' and its computed gap is 'normal'; the closing paragraph's className is 'mt-space-4 text-sm text-text-muted' and its computed margin-top is '0px'.

51 uses of the space-* family across 18 files in src/, all inert: gap-space-3 x6, px-space-4 x5, px-space-3 x4, p-space-4 x4, gap-space-2 x4, mt-space-4 x3, gap-space-4 x3, py-space-6 x2, py-space-2 x2, px-space-6 x2, p-space-6 x2, gap-space-1 x2, plus singles in top-space-2, py-space-8, px-space-2, mt-space-2, left-space-2, gap-space-6.

Why the obvious fix does not work, measured in Chromium: an inline <a> with min-height:44px measures 85x19; with the siblings' exact `min-height:44px; line-height:44px` it measures 167x19. min-height does not apply to a non-replaced inline box. Adding inline-flex + items-center takes the same element to 78x44.
Why min-width is required: the brand link measures 35px wide and QA's predicate at spec/a11y.spec.ts:56 filters on `c.h < 44 || c.w < 44`, so it fails on width as well as height.

docs/ui.md:225 states both clauses in one sentence — 'Touch targets are at least 44px by 44px, and no control is within 8px of another control's edge' — and QA's T-35 measures only the first. On the pre-fix build the second clause is violated app-wide: the top bar's Tabs→Groups→display-name→Sign out gaps all measured 0px against a declared gap-space-3 (12px).

Fix verified on a rebuilt 598cda8 with exactly the four edits in files[]: undersizedTargets() returns an empty list on all four screens; inter-control gaps are 36px/12px/16px down /sign-up and 36px/12px/16px down /sign-in with 12px across the top bar — the designed token values, which is the confirmation that the tokens now resolve.

No regressions from the same build: zero horizontal overflow at 360px on all four screens, exactly one h1 on / and /settings, sign-up still lands signed in on /, and vitest 81 passed / 7 files, tsc --noEmit exit 0, eslint exit 0.

align-middle was trialled and rejected: with the spacing tokens fixed it changed no measurement on either clause of docs/ui.md:225, so it was removed to keep the diff to three className edits plus one CSS block.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add min-h-[44px] to the three link call sites only, copying the classes their siblings already carry.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Measured, it does not work. These are inline anchors and min-height does not apply to a non-replaced inline box: the cross-links stay 16px tall and the brand link 24px. This is the patch that looks right and leaves T-35 red.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add min-h-[44px] plus inline-flex to the three links, and stop there — the minimal reading of BUG-1.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It satisfies the one assertion QA wrote while leaving the rule that assertion derives from broken. With the tokens still inert I measured the cross-link 0px from the submit button, so docs/ui.md:225's second clause stays violated app-wide and the top bar's controls stay 0px apart. It treats the symptom and leaves the cause.

alternatives_considered.approach: Rename the token family in the 51 call sites to Tailwind's bare numeric scale (gap-3, mt-4, px-6), leaving globals.css alone.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It works, at the cost of editing 18 files and discarding the property v1 was deliberate about — that a utility's name is the name in docs/ui.md's spacing table. The same fix is one six-line block in globals.css, and it keeps every call site readable as a token reference.

alternatives_considered.approach: Define both --space-N and --spacing-space-N, leaving the original tokens in place as well.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It makes the defect recur silently: the dead --space-N block would still read as authoritative to whoever writes the next token, and nothing would tell them it generates nothing.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add a lint rule or a unit test that fails when a theme namespace generates no utility.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Genuinely the right guard against a recurrence, and deliberately deferred rather than dismissed — it is a new mechanism with its own design questions, and this ticket's failure is fixed without it. Named in out_of_scope so the next ticket takes it as a decision instead of rediscovering it. The browser criterion AC-12 covers the same ground for this defect in the meantime.

alternatives_considered.approach: Rewrite the criterion AC-10, which QA's T-35 was derived from and which does not mention touch targets at all.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: AC-10 is not wrong — it is a summary criterion whose stated authority is docs/ui.md, and docs/ui.md:225 is unambiguous and correct. QA read past it to the real rule and found a real defect. Rewriting a correct criterion to match the code would be the one thing this stage must never do; adding AC-12 alongside it is the correct move.

assumptions: The pinned tailwindcss 4.3 in package.json behaves as 4.3.3 does in the isolation test; the version difference between them affects nothing here, since --spacing-* is the v4 namespace throughout the 4.x line.
docs/ui.md:225 is approved and unchangeable, so 44px/44px and the 8px separation are the fixed targets the code must meet.

QA's undersizedTargets() predicate — measuring a, button, input, select and textarea, excluding sr-only clips, filtering on w<44 || h<44 — is the definition of 'meets the minimum' this loop is held to, as it was for T-35.

The 8px separation clause is in scope. It is half of the same sentence of docs/ui.md as the clause QA tested, it is measurably violated today, and it is what the root cause produces — but if a maintainer reads it as out of scope for this ticket, the globals.css fix still stands on its own and only AC-12's second sentence would need narrowing.
unknowns: No prior QA run has ever asserted the 8px separation clause, so there is no historical record of it holding anywhere in the product. I have established today's baseline (12px top bar, 12-36px auth forms); whether some other screen has a subtler violation that only becomes visible once spacing starts resolving is not something this run can rule out — the fix makes those screens space out for the first time.
Whether the maintainer wants the lint rule or unit test that would catch an unresolvable theme namespace. Deferred to out_of_scope with the reasoning attached.

Whether any of the 15 other files using spacing utilities will now overflow or mis-lay-out at 360px or 200% zoom. Their spacing has never actually applied before, so this is the first time those layouts are exercised at all. The four screens QA covers were measured; the remaining primitives (Dialog, Skeleton, ErrorState, Money) have no callers yet and so cannot be measured until a later ticket renders them.
residual_risks: The CSS fix is invisible to every check CI runs. tsc, eslint and all 81 tests were green on the broken build and are green on the fixed one; only a browser can tell the two apart. That is why AC-12 is verify:'browser' and why its second sentence asks QA to check inter-control gaps explicitly rather than assuming T-35's passing covers it.

QA is given no memory of this run. AC-12 is written to be checked from scratch against a live browser, which is the only reason a confirmed bug cannot regress silently — the next run must measure both axes and both clauses without being told that this is what broke last time.

review.title: The ticket fixed one inert Tailwind token namespace in the @theme block and left a second, identical one three lines below it: `--radius: 8px` does not generate the `rounded-radius` utility any more than `--space-3` generated `gap-space-3`. Every button, input, card, dialog and skeleton in the product therefore renders with square corners, against docs/ui.md:27 ('Cards, inputs, buttons. One radius for the product'). The work order explicitly audited this block and recorded the opposite conclusion — files[0] says 'Change nothing else in the file: the ten colour tokens, the radius, the font stacks ... are all correct and all verified working.' The radius is not correct and was not working. This is the same root cause the ticket set out to eliminate, surviving in the same six lines, so the fix is incomplete against its own stated root cause rather than against a new requirement.
review.detail:
The ticket fixed one inert Tailwind token namespace in the @theme block and left a second, identical one three lines below it: `--radius: 8px` does not generate the `rounded-radius` utility any more than `--space-3` generated `gap-space-3`. Every button, input, card, dialog and skeleton in the product therefore renders with square corners, against docs/ui.md:27 ('Cards, inputs, buttons. One radius for the product'). The work order explicitly audited this block and recorded the opposite conclusion — files[0] says 'Change nothing else in the file: the ten colour tokens, the radius, the font stacks ... are all correct and all verified working.' The radius is not correct and was not working. This is the same root cause the ticket set out to eliminate, surviving in the same six lines, so the fix is incomplete against its own stated root cause rather than against a new requirement.

`src/app/globals.css:33`

Evidence: Isolated against the pinned tailwindcss 4.3.3: a @theme block containing only `--radius: 8px`, with markup using `rounded-radius`, emits zero occurrences of `rounded-radius` and emits only `.rounded { border-radius: var(--radius) }`; adding `--radius-radius: 8px` alongside it makes `.rounded-radius` appear. Compiling the PR's real src/app/globals.css against the real class names in src/ gives `grep -cF rounded-radius` = 0. The production build agrees: `grep -cF rounded-radius /tmp/pr13/.next/static/chunks/*.css` = 0. Measured in Chromium against the running build on /sign-in: getComputedStyle(button).borderRadius = '0px', getComputedStyle(input).borderRadius = '0px', getComputedStyle(card).borderRadius = '0px', while getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).getPropertyValue('--radius') = '8px' — so the token is emitted to :root (which is why the hand-written focus ring at globals.css:76 works and looks right) while every utility built on its name emits nothing. Six call sites carry the dead class: src/components/ui/button.tsx:48, button.tsx:82, card.tsx:9, dialog.tsx:76, input.tsx:34, skeleton.tsx:6. The defect predates this PR — it is present at 17bd4ee — so this PR neither caused nor claimed it; the finding is that the fix's own audit of the @theme block reached the wrong conclusion about it and left it.

Fix: Rename the token to the v4 border-radius namespace so the six existing call sites resolve unchanged, mirroring exactly what was done for spacing: `--radius-radius: 8px`. globals.css:76 reads `border-radius: var(--radius)` directly, so that reference must be updated to `var(--radius-radius)` at the same time, or the focus ring silently loses its radius. Verify on the built CSS that `.rounded-radius { border-radius: var(--radius-radius) }` is emitted, and re-measure getComputedStyle(...).borderRadius on a button, an input and a card in Chromium — expecting '8px', not '0px'.

`src/app/layout.tsx:18`

Evidence: Measured in Chromium against the running build on / at 360px: after `document.querySelector('a[href="#main"]').focus()`, getBoundingClientRect() returns width 146, height 40, with computed clip 'auto' and visibility 'visible' — i.e. it is genuinely visible once focused, and 40 < 44. The class list at layout.tsx:20 is `sr-only focus:not-sr-only focus:absolute focus:left-space-2 focus:top-space-2 focus:z-10 focus:bg-surface focus:px-space-3 focus:py-space-2`, which carries py-space-2 (8px each side) plus a 24px line box and no min-h. QA's own predicate excludes sr-only clips, and an unfocused skip link is one, so T-35 correctly did not report it and the current run will not either; it is reported here because the ticket's stated approach was to grep the callers rather than fix the named sites, and this is a caller that was missed.

Fix: Give the focused skip link the same minimum as the other three: add `inline-flex min-h-[44px] min-w-[44px] items-center` to the className at layout.tsx:20. It is sr-only until focused, so this changes nothing for sighted mouse users and costs nothing visually. Confirm by focusing it in Chromium and re-measuring that both axes are at least 44.

review.detail:
Patterns: .sdlc/memory/patterns/ is an empty README and this bug is the exact shape the directory exists to catch. A Tailwind v4 @theme token declared under a namespace the version does not generate utilities from fails SILENTLY — tsc, eslint and vitest were all green on the broken build, and it survived a full review — and the same mistake is sitting in the file the ticket just edited, in a second namespace (--radius), still unmade. Whoever next opens globals.css will read --spacing-space-3 as proof the block was audited, and it was, and the answer was wrong once. A 'silent dead token' entry would cost one file and would have caught both.

`.sdlc/memory/patterns/:1`

Evidence: `.sdlc/memory/patterns/README.md` is the only file in the directory and its body is 'Empty for now. It fills as the system works.' — which is now false, this is the system working. The index line reads 'patterns/ — bug shapes this repo has produced before. Grep by symptom.' The symptom that fits both halves of this ticket: 'a UI utility class compiles to no rule and nothing complains'. I reproduced it directly against the pinned tailwindcss 4.3.3: a @theme block declaring only `--space-3: 12px` emits zero occurrences of `gap-space-3`; the same token as `--spacing-space-3` emits `.gap-space-3 { gap: var(--spacing-space-3); }`. Compiling the PR's real src/app/globals.css against every .ts/.tsx on the branch gives `grep -c 'gap-space-3'` = 1 and `grep -c 'rounded-radius'` = 0 — the same block, one namespace right and one namespace wrong, in the file this PR edited. The work order's own confidence_rationale records that 'all three were green on the broken build'. The library file should be named for the symptom, per that README's own instruction.

Fix: Add .sdlc/memory/patterns/silent-dead-theme-token.md: symptom (a class written in JSX produces no CSS rule and no tool complains), cause (a @theme key outside v4's generating namespaces — `--space-*` for spacing, `--radius` for border-radius — is emitted as a plain custom property and generates nothing), how it was found (only by compiling the real stylesheet and grepping for the class name, or by measuring in a browser; nothing CI runs observes it), and the check (compile globals.css with the real content set and assert each token in the block has at least one emitted rule). Naming it by symptom is what the README asks for, so a future agent grepping 'no rule' or 'not applied' finds it.
